name: Meter Passport BSC handler credits untransferred wrapped-native deposits

classification.summary: Meter's ChainBridge fork added a wrapped-native path to ERC20Handler.deposit(bytes32,uint8,uint64,address,bytes) that skips the token movement entirely for the configured wtoken: `// ether case, the weth already in handler, do nothing` guards `if (tokenAddress != _wtokenAddress) { burnERC20 | lockERC20 }`. That assumption only holds for Bridge.depositETH, which requires `amount == msg.value - fee` and wraps the value itself. Bridge.deposit stayed callable for the same resourceID and requires only `msg.value == fee`, so any caller could write a DepositRecord and emit Deposit for an arbitrary WBNB amount without transferring anything, and the relayer set released or minted that amount on the destination chain.

loss.notes: Two components, both caused by BSC-executed deposits. (1) The anchor deposit credited 3632.795971816270126503 WBNB without transferring anything; 39 seconds later the relayer set executed the matching proposal on BSC itself (destinationChainID 4 is BSC's own Passport id) and ERC20Handler 0x5945241bbb68b4454bb67bd2b069e74c09ac3d51 sent exactly 3632795971816270126503 wei of native BNB to the attacker in 0xf70b4aa715c0a04079c56cd9036cc63cdb6101e400520a8f2c019ad2ced5358e, an exact depletion of the handler's wrapped-native reserve, valued at the WBNB observation nearest the anchor. (2) Two further BSC deposits of 15000 WBNB each to destinationChainID 5 (Moonriver) minted 30000 unbacked BNB.bsc to the attacker on Moonriver, which he sold into the single SushiSwap BNB.bsc/ETH pair over six swaps for exactly 338.181429214488085156 ETH. Those sales moved BNB.bsc from a 422.88 USD spot mark to a realised 34.35 USD per token, so the realised proceeds are used and the method is "other"; spot-marking 30000 BNB would imply 12.7M USD at a price at which the position could not be sold. Excluded from this record: 398850.18169558374 BUSD that the same BSC handler released to the attacker in 0xe045c40c51250ef611f06c4f11ab4ea11486cd8f6827ed03eb06ad4c8c6cf53e and 0x3fb520c6b44dcbf18fcd75757883a158e6b075420225e01b6761b6a2645157eb, because those proposals originate from deposits executed on Passport source chain 3 rather than on BSC; the separate Ethereum-leg deposits on Bridge 0xa2a22b46b8df38cd7c55e6bf32ea5a32637cf2b1; and Hundred Finance's roughly 3.3M USD of knock-on borrowing losses, which are a third party's oracle exposure to the crashed Moonriver BNB price.

lastCodeChange.description: ERC20Handler is a non-upgradeable contract created directly by an EOA. Its runtime hashes to 0x051166e9379a6663dc05e5fd97aec94411bd05cb1aeea836046d12df2b02efa3 both at the deployment block 7848927 and at block 14992189 immediately before the exploit, so the defect-bearing bytecode is unchanged over the whole interval.

sources.note: Chain established from the attacker's own transactions: EOA 0x8d3d13cac607b7297ff61a5e1e71072758af4d01 made four Bridge.deposit calls on BSC Bridge 0xfd55ebc7bbde603a048648c6eab8775c997c1001, each paying only the 0.008 BNB fee. The first, 0xc4d7e160c7652f2db22681aa2777c5b37937bf30375c5b2c6b2bd172ae984950 at 14990769:105, used the MTRG resource and correctly burned 136.0992633577453 MTRG, so it does not execute the defect. The anchor 0x63f37aff7e40b85b0a6b3fd414389f6011cc09b276dc8e13b6afa19061f7ed8e at 14992190:112, timestamp 1644070960, status 1, is the first deposit using the WBNB resource 0x0000000000000000000000bb4cdb9cbd36b01bd1cbaebf2de08d9173bc095c01 with a calldata amount of 3632795971816270126503; its callTracer shows Bridge -> ERC20Handler 0x5945241bbb68b4454bb67bd2b069e74c09ac3d51 with no inner token call at all, against the MTRG deposit whose trace contains a burnFrom. Read the Etherscan-verified ERC20Handler source: the wrapped-native branch is `if (tokenAddress != _wtokenAddress) { ... }` with the comment `ether case, the weth already in handler, do nothing`, and Bridge.deposit only requires `msg.value == fee` while Bridge.depositETH requires `amount == msg.value - fee` and performs the wrap itself. Boundary test: with _wtokenAddress set to any real wrapped-native token the function is wrong for every caller and every amount, and the only configuration that makes it safe is disabling the feature, so this is an executable-code defect and not a parameter. Code history: Etherscan getcontractcreation puts the handler at 7848927:96 in 0x3b9b52026a374f5c3e115df18e88c120efba7503c25f42a0837046b429dba52d from 0xbb245d5c1d504dd5295b12b90963fd26b06bc743, timestamp 1622345639; eth_getCode at block 7848927 and at block 14992189 both hash to 0x051166e9379a6663dc05e5fd97aec94411bd05cb1aeea836046d12df2b02efa3 and the contract is not a proxy, so codeAgeSeconds = 1644070960 - 1622345639 = 21725321 (251.4 d). Loss reconstructed from receipts: internal transfer of 3632795971816270126503 wei native BNB from the handler to the attacker in 0xf70b4aa715c0a04079c56cd9036cc63cdb6101e400520a8f2c019ad2ced5358e at block 14992203; two further BSC deposits of 15000 WBNB each to Passport chain 5 followed by two 15000 BNB.bsc mints from the zero address on Moonriver at blocks 1442439 and 1442487, and six SushiSwap sales on Moonriver returning 272376308003477609054 + 7538526063981057562 + 15283568631316749045 + 14960274174613810125 + 23299408459100801796 + 4723343881998057574 = 338181429214488085156 wei of ETH, of which 338.181 was bridged out. Passport chain ids read from the contracts: BSC Bridge _chainID() = 4, Ethereum Bridge 0xa2a22b46b8df38cd7c55e6bf32ea5a32637cf2b1 _chainID() = 1.

limitations: The 30000 BNB.bsc component is realised on Moonriver (eip155:1285), which the onchain verifier is not wired for; its quantities were reproduced through the Etherscan v2 Moonriver endpoint rather than by scripts/verify.mjs.

notes: The same defect was exercised on the Ethereum deployment of Meter Passport (Bridge 0xa2a22b46b8df38cd7c55e6bf32ea5a32637cf2b1, deposits 0x2d3987963b77159cfe4f820532d729b0364c7f05511f23547765c75b110b629c and 0xdfea6413c7eb3068093dcbbe65bcc9ba635e227c35e57fe482bb5923c89e31f7 for 422.5087086393632 and 1500 WETH). That is a separate same-day campaign against a different deployment and belongs in its own record.
